# OpenVector

> OpenVector is a free, open-source (MIT) raster-to-vector converter. It traces PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP and TIFF images into editable SVG, PDF, EPS, AI, DXF and EMF vectors. The online editor at https://openvector.app/editor/ runs entirely in the browser as WebAssembly, so images are never uploaded. The same Rust engine ships as a desktop app (Windows, macOS, Linux) and as a CLI and Node.js library on npm.

Key facts:

- Price: free. No account, watermark or export limit.
- Privacy: images stay in the browser tab's memory and are discarded when the tab closes.
- Tools: automatic tracing, manual palettes, segmentation editing, background removal, batch conversion (desktop and CLI).
- Browser requirements: current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari with WebAssembly threads and WebGL2. First visit downloads about 5 MB.
- Current version: 0.1.5. Author: Microck.

## Product

- [OpenVector home](https://openvector.app/): what it does, supported formats and FAQ
- [Online editor](https://openvector.app/editor/): convert an image in the browser
- [Desktop downloads](https://github.com/Microck/openvector/releases/latest): Windows, macOS and Linux packages
